newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks surge three percent to record close.
newsitem.headline: French stocks surge three percent to record close.

text.p: French stocks surged three percent on Wednesday to an all-time closing high, powered by gains on Wall Street, a rebound in the dollar and higher bond prices.
The bourse's blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 82.68 points, or 2.97 percent, at 2,867.44, and the CAC-40 June futures contract rose 68 points to 2,844.
The CAC index's previous closing record of 2,808.52 points was set on June 13.
The market's rise was helped by a rally in banking stocks after Compagnie Bancaire proposed to buy out minority holders in finance firms Cardif and Locabail.
Volume continued heavy, with a hefty 14.66 billion francs changing hands. Block trades with dividend stripping helped boost market liquidity.

* Banking and financial stocks starred. Cie Bancaire closed up 6.83 percent at 735 francs, on the back of its buy out offer for finance houses Cardif and UFB Locabail. Several brokers raised earnings forecasts for Bancaire, judging the move as earnings positive.
* Cie Financiere Paribas gained 4.16 percent to 403.2 francs. Brokers believe the holding company has more restructuring moves in the pipeline.
Among the moves being talked about in the market are Paribas selling Bancaire or Cetelem, or even the buyout of Cetelem, but the latter option is considered expensive.
* The market had been expecting some sort of shake-up in the Bancaire group for some time.
* Among bank stocks benefiting from the Bancaire move were Societe Generale, up 4.23 percent at 665 francs, BNP up 3.78 percent at 244.2.
* Among stocks catching up were Thomson-CSF, climbing 4.52 percent to 159.6, after falling heavily last week.

* Saint-Gobain rose 3.22 percent to 865 francs. Chairman Jean-Louis Beffa gave an upbeat presentation to the annual shareholders meeting, forecasting the group would have its best ever year in 1997, with strong profit growth excluding capital gains.
* Synthelabo, up 1.49 percent at 750, and L'Oreal, up 4.79 percent at 2,452, saw active trading with blocks of stock changing hands.
* LVMH, up 1.89 percent at 1,511, said it added 0.07 percent to its Grand Met stake yesterday, and now holds a total 6.37 percent.

* Pechiney chairman Jean-Pierre Rodier told shareholders that the operating margin would be much higher in the second half of 1997 than the year-earlier level. Stock in the aluminium company closed up 4.73 percent at 232.5.

* Cap Gemini lagged the market with a rise of 0.73 percent to 345 francs. Daimler-Benz said in Germany it no longer planned to take over the French computer systems house and would sell its 24.4 percent stake in the medium term through a convertible bond.
